data.title: Trump prepares tariff relief on Canada ahead of midterms - report
data.description:
The Trump administration is preparing to eliminate 50% tariffs on select Canadian agricultural and forestry imports in a bid to shield Sen. Susan Collins (R., Maine) and other border-state Republicans ahead of the midterm elections, according to a media report published Friday.

The forthcoming presidential proclamation could be signed as early as Friday, although the scope and timing could change, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

Still, the administration may offset the relief by levying new duties on other Canadian goods, the WSJ noted.

The cross-border dispute started in late August, when the White House invoked Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act—commonly known as Smoot-Hawley—to penalize Canadian imports, prompting retaliatory measures from Ottawa and threats of further auto tariffs.

The planned exemptions are aimed mainly at boosting Collins, who is locked in a neck-and-neck race against Democrat Troy Jackson. Jackson has made the trade war a central campaign theme in Maine, where border commerce is key.

The prospective tariff overhaul comes amid mounting pushback, with a New Jersey food importer filing a lawsuit this week challenging the legality of using Smoot-Hawley powers for the levies.

Prediction market Kalshi has a 67% chance of a Democratic sweep of Congress in the midterms, pricing unified Democratic control well ahead of divided government or a Republican sweep.

A White House official dismissed advance reports of tariff adjustments as speculation, while the U.S. Trade Representative’s office declined to comment, the Journal said.

data.title: GE Vernova Stocks Edge Lower Before $176 Billion Backlog Checkpoint
data.description:
Power-equipment group GE Vernova faces a cash-conversion test at next week's earnings, with shares edging lower 0.19% to $825.87 at 11:35 a.m. ET on October 23. Investor's Business Daily linked concerns about the stock to Meta's latest earnings and AI spending economics ahead of the October 28 report, due before the opening bell. The investor question is straightforward: how much of the AI power boom becomes durable cash?

The company's second-quarter results put backlog at $176 billion, with $24.2 billion in orders against $11.1 billion in revenue. Data-center orders topped $5 billion through June. Management's full-year outlook calls for revenue of $45.5 billion$46.5 billion and free cash flow of $11.5 billion$12.5 billion. Those midpoints imply cash generation equal to roughly 26.1% of revenue. That makes the sources and timing of cash receipts worth watching closely.

Big orders create opportunity. Deliveries determine how much of it reaches earnings. The financial snapshot shows a GF Score of just 17/100, a cautionary counterweight to the enormous backlog, though the score alone does not explain the underlying risks. At the next report, investors should examine customer advances, order conversion and progress toward turbine-production targets. Strong deposits can lift cash before equipment ships; sustained execution must eventually support that cash generation. The useful test is whether deliveries, margins and cash flow advance together.

data.title: James Russell Pushes for Changes at Abeona Therapeutics with 6.1% Stake
data.description:
James Russell Pushes for Changes at Abeona Therapeutics with 6.1% Stake

James Russell, through the James Russell Revocable Trust, reported a 6.1% stake in Abeona Therapeutics Inc. In a Schedule 13D filed Oct. 23, 2026, Russell shifted from passive reporting after deciding to pursue a more active role. He cited concerns about the company’s operations and governance and raised the possibility of board and leadership changes.

Investor Intent

Russell began raising concerns with Abeona Therapeutics’ management and board in May 2026. On Oct. 14, he met with two directors and urged the board to consider adding independent directors and exploring a change in executive leadership. The next day, a director told him the full board had heard his concerns.

Russell plans to keep engaging with management and the board. Depending on the board’s response, he could nominate director candidates for the 2027 annual meeting, oppose incumbent directors, speak with other shareholders, or seek board representation. He also says he will not vote shares he acquired on or after Oct. 15 at company meetings.

Investor's Background

The James Russell Revocable Trust is a Nevada trust that holds investments for its beneficiaries. Russell serves as the trust’s sole trustee and controls its voting and investment decisions; he also works as vice president of Performance Steel Inc. The trust bought its shares with personal funds, spending about $17.8 million in total, including about $3.7 million on shares acquired since its prior filing.

Original SEC Filing: ABEONA THERAPEUTICS INC. [ ABEO ] - SCHEDULE 13D - Oct. 23, 2026

That could expand Cisco's opportunity, but the announcement does not establish how much additional revenue this design will deliver.

The valuation leaves little room for weak execution: the GF Value comparison puts the shares 40.93% above its $75.61 estimate. That premium raises the bar for converting AI demand into revenue. Investors should watch for named production deployments, measurable service performance and identifiable equipment, software or support spending. A bigger role in AI networking matters most when it produces bigger sales.

data.title: on!® Crowns Team Grass League Champions at Inaugural on!vitational™ Golf Tournament
data.description:
Helix Innovations LLC, an operating company of Altria Group, Inc. (Altria) (), today announced the winners of on!® nicotine pouches’ inaugural on!vitational, held October 16 and 17 at TGL’s SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida. The two-day golf and entertainment experience brought together eight teams of current and former professional athletes, golf personalities, entertainers and adult nicotine consumers age 25+ for a competition that combined golf, technology and entertainment.

Well-known golf influencer Paige Spiranac and Team Grass League, including former professional golfer Drew Kittleson and Grass League co-founder Jimmy Hoselton, captured the inaugural on!vitational Championship. The team defeated former PGA TOUR veteran Ricky Barnes and Team Troon in a dramatic final to claim the tournament trophy and golf’s orangest jacket. After teams including Malbon, Palm Tree Crew and Hypegolf battled throughout the competition, Grass League staged a thrilling comeback, with an on!® consumer sweepstakes winner delivering a pivotal shot on the penultimate hole to help secure the victory.

Unlike traditional golf tournaments, the on!vitational put nicotine consumers 25+ directly into the competition alongside some of the biggest personalities in golf, sports and entertainment. Consumer participants, selected at random through an on!® sweepstakes earlier this year, competed as members of the eight teams. The two-day event was emceed by popular golf influencer and TGL host Roger Steele.

Grass League co-founder Jimmy Hoselton summed up the excitement: “on!® has been with us from the beginning. We're all in on on!®, and we're all in on the on!vitational.”

A New Kind of Golf Competition

Held inside TGL’s 250,000-square-foot SoFi Center, the on!vitational took advantage of the venue’s technology, including its over four-story tall simulator screen and real-life putting and short-game areas, to deliver a golf experience unlike a traditional tournament.

The competition also featured unique in-match opportunities. Momentum Swing allowed the sweepstakes winners to chip into designated round spots on the green for significant bonus points while Celeb Shot allowed teams to choose any team member to take a shot, regardless of whose turn it was. All Axis offered a strategic element where teams could move the green 45 or 90 degrees in any direction after their opponent was on or close to the green to gain short game and putting advantages at key moments.

These elements ended up being major factors in the final. Grass League was down 6-0 on No. 6. They used their Celeb Shot to allow Kittleson to hit, and he delivered. He chipped it in from off the green to give Grass League their first points of the match. A 20-foot birdie putt on No. 7 by Hoselton pulled Team Grass League within two points, and the Momentum Swing was the deciding factor. Trailing 6-4 on No. 8, Team Grass League sweepstakes winner William K. chipped it into one of the designated spots, scoring six points, and clinching the comeback Championship victory.

"This was one of the best experiences of my life," said on!® sweepstakes and Team Grass League winner William K. in a post-match interview. "My team kept picking me up throughout the tournament, and I was able to deliver when it counted. Really thankful to on!® for putting on such a great event."

Beyond the competition, multi-platinum recording artist Flo Rida headlined Saturday's entertainment, bringing an energy-filled conclusion to two great days of golf. He performed some of his biggest hits and invited tournament winners and guests to join him onstage.

Honoring Veterans Through Golf

The on!vitational also featured a partnership with the Veteran Golfers Association (VGA), a nonprofit dedicated to enriching the lives of veterans and their family members through the camaraderie and sportsmanship of golf.

In addition to competing as one of the tournament's eight teams, the VGA participated in a special military salute recognizing U.S. Navy veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Edward C. Byers Jr., who attended the event. All proceeds from can sales at the on!vitational went towards supporting the VGA and its mission.

Relive the on!vitational

Fans 21 or older can relive the competition, winning moments, player highlights and entertainment through content available on the on!® Instagram.

About on!® Nicotine Pouches

on!® and on! PLUS® nicotine pouches are designed for adult nicotine consumers 21+ looking for a satisfying, premium nicotine pouch experience. With six varieties and three nicotine strengths, on!® nicotine pouches deliver against a wide variety of adult consumer 21+ tastes and preferences. on! PLUS® nicotine pouches are designed with a proprietary NICOSILK™ mesh technology for a comfortable feel. on! PLUS® is available in Mint, Wintergreen & Tobacco flavors at 6, 9 and 12 mg strengths. on! PLUS® will also offer the same three strength options in exciting new flavors: Blueberry Mint, Mango Pineapple and Watermelon Mint (select stores only).

Helix Innovations LLC Profile

Helix Innovations LLC (Helix), an Altria company, offers a portfolio of oral nicotine pouch products for adult nicotine consumers 21+, including on!® and on! PLUS®. In December 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration authorized the marketing of certain on! PLUS® variants.

Helix is committed to responsible marketing and preventing underage access to nicotine products. As an Altria operating company, Helix follows marketing practices designed to appeal to adult nicotine consumers 21+ while taking steps to limit reach to underage audiences.

No one under the age of 21 should use nicotine products. Nicotine is addictive, and nicotine products are not risk-free. on!® products are intended for adult nicotine consumers 21+.

data.title: Swiss Market Ends Moderately Lower
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - After edging up a bit at the start, the Swiss market retreated and stayed in negative territory throughout the session on Friday, as investors reacted to corporate earnings announcements and continued to follow geopolitical news.

Worries about inflation and possible monetary tightening by several global central banks rendered the mood cautious.

The benchmark SMI settled with a loss of 85.61 points or 0.59% at 14,462.36, off the day's low of 14,408.96.

Richemont ended nearly 6.5% down. Helvetia Baloise Holding ended 2.76% down. Sika drifted lower by 2.3%. VAT Group and ABB dropped by about 1.7% and 1.6%, respectively.

Julius Baer, Nestle, Novartis, Zurich Insurance and Swiss Life Holding ended down 0.4%-0.1%.

Holcim moved up 5%. The building materials firm's EBIT reached 976 million Swiss francs in the third quarter, up 16.8% from 836 million francs in the prior year quarter, with organic growth of 12.2%. The recurring EBIT margin expanded to 20.9% from 20.7% a year ago.

Net sales totaled 4.662 billion francs, up 15.5% from 4.036 billion francs in the same quarter last year, representing organic growth of 5.1%.

Galderma Group, Partners Group, Sandoz Group, Schindler Ps, Straumann Holding and SGS gained 1.8%-2.4%.

Logitech International, Kuehne + Nagel, Amrie, Geberit, Sonova and Lonza Group also closed on firm note.

data.title: Oil markets are on edge ahead of the weekend, as midterm elections near and fresh U.S. strikes on Iran are predicted
data.description:
By Isabel Wang and Myra P. Saefong

Global oil prices are closing in on their highest levels since the Iran war began

Oil has climbed back to an Iran-war high and may soon go higher, if the U.S. and Israel strike Iran after their respective voters go to the polls in the coming days.

Eight months into the Iran war, the global energy crisis is showing no signs of easing. Instead, oil prices were surging again, hurtling toward their highest levels since the conflict began in February and stoking fears that the world is heading toward an even more punishing energy crunch.

"Worries about oil back over $100 a barrel and the Iran conflict flaring up again are top of mind heading into the weekend," said Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group.

Global Brent crude for December delivery (BRN00) (BRNZ26) jumped 3.4% to $111.44 a barrel Friday afternoon, putting the benchmark within striking distance of its wartime settlement high of $118.35, reached in late March. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery (CL.1) (CLZ26) also climbed 3.5% to $103.09 a barrel. It settled as high as $112.95 in April, its highest level since the Iran war began, according to FactSet data.

The recent uptick in oil prices comes as the Iran-backed Houthis conducted further drone strikes Wednesday on Saudi airports and the Saudi Aramco Shaybah oil field, attacks that earlier this week led the U.S. to order embassy staff in Riyadh to leave the country. Trump has warned that the U.S. could attack Iran anew after the Nov. 3 midterm elections, and both the U.S. and Israel have been preparing options for strikes after voters go to the polls. Israel holds its elections on Tuesday.

Another risk for energy markets: Iran said that if U.S. and Israeli bombings resume, Tehran will respond with strikes on pipelines and airports in oil-rich Persian Gulf countries, according to Wall Street Journal reporting.

"Iran is agitating to keep oil prices high and push down American popular support for the Trump administration and the war," said Matt Gertken, chief geopolitical and U.S. political strategist at BCA Research. "But after the election President Trump will intensify strikes to try to coerce Iran's leaders into a ceasefire."

Trump on Thursday hinted at fresh action against Iran during a speech in Iowa.

"We're going to have Iran finished very soon," he said in Sioux City. "One way or the other, it's going to be done very soon, and your gasoline prices and your oil is going to come tumbling down."

Anna Kelly, a White House spokeswoman, said in an emailed response to MarketWatch on Friday that the U.S. will not be attacking Iran "at any time" prior to the midterm elections.

"As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait," she said.

But oil's climb back toward its wartime highs is more than a geopolitical story. It's the clearest sign yet of how exposed Trump and the Republicans are to the one issue they can't spin: the price at the pump. The national average price for a gallon of regular gasoline is $4.29, according to AAA. That's up from less than $3 a gallon before the war.

It's a test not just for a stock market already juggling earnings, an upcoming interest-rate decision from the Federal Reserve and mounting worries about debt related to the artificial-intelligence build-out, but also for Trump and his party, who have staked so much on the economy ahead of a crucial moment that could shape the direction of the president's final two years in office.

Beyond a possible fresh U.S. attack on Iran, the post-midterm outlook is cloudy. Democrats appear poised to take control of at least one chamber of Congress and have pledged to try to wind down the Iran war. But they're unlikely to win enough seats to override a Trump veto of a bill that would restrict military operations, as a longtime national security expert wrote in a CNN analysis.

Trump, for his part, has taken steps to ease the pressure on energy markets, including temporarily allowing Russia to supply diesel to U.S. and other markets and announcing plans to use Defense Production Act funding to expand oil production and refining.

That move opens up money for oil projects, but it takes years to build a refinery. So really, "this is a policy for the 2030 diesel market," Giacomo Prandelli, a commodity analyst and geopolitical strategist and the writer of a newsletter called Merchant's News, said on X. Voters will soon go to the polls, and they "pay today's prices."

"The oil market isn't pricing availability alone. It's pricing reliability," said Angie Gildea, global head of oil and gas at KPMG, in comments to MarketWatch. "Even when barrels are flowing, concerns about energy infrastructure and shipping routes can keep a risk premium in prices."

With no end to the Iran conflict in sight, market analysts see oil prices staying elevated even in the aftermath of the midterms.

Brent crude could remain in the range of $110 to $120 a barrel for a while, further increasing inflation risks, said Fawad Razaqzada, global macroeconomic market analyst at StoneX Trading and Forex.com. "That in turn could be bad news for all sorts of risk assets," he told MarketWatch on Friday.

Gertken at BCA Research said consumers can handle oil prices that average $105 a barrel over the coming months, but not an increase to $160. However, should oil reach $160 a barrel, the Trump administration might try "toppling the Iranian regime," he said. "So Iran will probably not drive prices that high."

He expects to see U.S. strikes intensifying in the coming months, and then both the U.S. and Iran opting for negotiations due to a "lack of economic and political capabilities to support a longer war."

Both the U.S. and global oil benchmarks have risen for three consecutive weeks and on Friday were on pace for their biggest three-week advance since early September, according to FactSet data.

Robert Schroeder and Joy Wiltermuth contributed.

-Isabel Wang -Myra P. Saefong

data.title: Tech Stocks Roar Back as Nasdaq Nears Erasing Its Weekly Loss
data.description:
U.S. technology shares rebounded in late-morning trading Friday, pushing the Nasdaq Composite into positive territory while the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 remained lower.

The recovery brought the tech-heavy index close to wiping out its weekly decline.

The Nasdaq gained 79 points, or 0.3%, after falling as much as 0.5% shortly after the opening bell. Technology buying picked up as the session progressed, lifting the benchmark from its early pullback. The recovery erased its earlier losses for the session.

The State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF climbed 1% by 11:32 a.m. Eastern time, reversing an early decline of as much as 0.4%. The turnaround showed that renewed demand for technology shares was helping lift the sector fund alongside the Nasdaq.

Gains remained concentrated, however, with the Dow and S&P 500 still lower. The divergence suggested the rebound had yet to spread across the broader market. The Nasdaq's move toward erasing its weekly loss marked a shift from the morning's weakness, although the latest figures did not indicate whether the recovery would last through the closing bell.

data.title: Dr Reddy’s launches two new semaglutide brands amid Obeda supply disruptions
data.description:
Dr Reddy’s Laboratories has expanded its portfolio of generic versions of Ozempic with two new brands to fill a supply-chain hit to its original Obeda injections, product photographs and marketing materials reviewed by Reuters show.

The shift, first reported here by Reuters, follows supply disruptions that hit sales of Dr Reddy’s Obeda injection in India’s fast-growing market for semaglutide, which is the active ingredient in Novo Nordisk’s weight-loss drug Wegovy.

Shares in Dr Reddy’s fell by as much as 2% after the Reuters report, before paring some losses to settle 1.4% lower.

Dr Reddy’s launched Obeda, a generic version of Novo Nordisk’s diabetes drug, in India in March and later in Canada after semaglutide lost patent protection, setting off a race among domestic drugmakers to launch lower-cost versions.

Manufacturing issues prompt production shift

The drugmaker said at a media briefing on Friday that after encountering manufacturing issues with Obeda in July, it had shifted production to a partner’s facility to maintain supplies.

Dr Reddy’s said that its Obeda Pro and Obeda Plus would remain available in the market and could be used for diabetes treatment and weight management.

Obeda Pro and Obeda Plus are manufactured by a different firm than the Obeda injectable, supplies of which were halted after Dr Reddy’s found an impurity in the active ingredient.

Several distributors told Reuters that Dr Reddy’s is likely to discontinue Obeda and will focus on Obeda Pro and Obeda Plus.

“The company said there were some technical issues with Obeda injectable, and they recalled stocks from us. They said they would instead supply Obeda Pro,” a drug distributor said.

“When we started off on semaglutide, we basically had two sources for the product. One was our own product and one through the partner product,” M.V. Ramana, chief executive of Global Generics, said on Friday.

Having multiple semaglutide brands should not be interpreted as evidence of one replacing another, the company told Reuters earlier.

Obeda injections recalled over impurity concerns

A company notice reviewed by Reuters showed Dr Reddy’s recalled Obeda injections in July “for technical evaluation”. An oral version of the drug was not recalled.

The company had also recalled batches of generic semaglutide in Canada in August because of the impurity issue. It will relaunch the drug in Canada this quarter and is targeting launches in Latin America and Africa in coming months.

Dr Reddy’s said in July that supplies of Obeda injections would be unavailable until November and analysts warned it risked losing market share if supplies were not restored soon.

On Friday, Dr Reddy’s said it was on track to resolve the impurity issue and relaunch next month.

Obeda Pro and Obeda Plus manufactured by Hetero Labs

Packaging materials showed Obeda was manufactured by contract manufacturer OneSource Specialty Pharma.

Obeda Pro and Obeda Plus, which began appearing in the market in late July according to supply invoices reviewed by Reuters, are manufactured by Hetero Labs.

Both are available in different dose strengths, just like Ozempic and Wegovy.

Hetero Labs and OneSource Specialty Pharma did not respond to requests for comment.

India’s semaglutide market expected to expand

Research firm Pharmarack estimated in March that the domestic market for semaglutide drugs will grow to 80 billion rupees ($844 million) by 2030.

Dr Reddy’s had sold about 442,000 units of generic semaglutide in India through September, research firm Pharmarack said. By comparison, India’s largest drugmaker Sun Pharma sold 151,000 semaglutide units.

data.title: Procter & Gamble Stocks Decrease 2.62% as $1.4 Billion Cost Burden Grows
data.description:
Consumer-products giant Procter & Gamble faces a bigger squeeze from input costs, with shares at $161.25, down 2.62% at 11:39 a.m. ET on October 23. According to Reuters, management raised its projected fiscal 2027 commodity-cost burden to $1.4 billion from $1 billiona 40% increase. Demand improved. Turning those extra sales into profit is proving harder.

P&G's quarterly results show organic sales grew 4%, with volume contributing 2.4 percentage points, product mix adding 1.1 points and pricing supplying just 0.4 points, subject to rounding. Revenue reached $23.3 billion, while core earnings increased only 1% to $2 per share. The pressure shows up in margins: core operating margin contracted 80 basis points despite 250 basis points of productivity savings. Selling more helped, but savings and modest price increases could not absorb the full cost squeeze.

The valuation picture shows shares trading 4.06% below the $168.07 GF Value estimatea modest discount that leaves limited room for disappointment. Management maintained its annual organic sales growth outlook of 1%3% and core earnings guidance of $6.89$7.11 per share. The test now is whether stronger demand can deliver better margins. With pricing contributing little, productivity needs to keep doing the heavy lifting.
